name: Angela Leong
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2011-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Hurun China (2021-2026)
forbes_bio: Angela Leong is co-chairman and the largest individual shareholder of casino company SJM Holdings. She is also an elected Macau legislator.
Hong Kong-listed SJM Holdings operates casino resorts including L'Arc and the Grand Lisboa Palace Resort in Macau.
She is the fourth wife of the late Stanley Ho, who started Sociedade de Turismo e Diversoes de Macau, or STDM, which controls SJM Holdings.
Leong, who started investing in her early 20s, also has a large portfolio of Hong Kong properties, to which she owes the vast majority of her wealth.
forbes_facts: Leong came from a wealthy army family, but things changed when her father died in 1974. She joined a dance school partly for the free accommodation, as her family had to move out of government housing.
In 1986, Leong met Macau legend Stanley Ho, now deceased, through his brother, who had been attending her dance class.

name: Premchand Godha
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2021-2025); Hurun Global (2021-2026); Hurun India (2015-2019)
forbes_bio: Premchand Godha is chairman of generics firm Ipca Labs, which manufactures formulations, bulk drugs and drug intermediates.
Godha acquired Ipca Labs together with the family of Bollywood superstar Amitabh Bachchan in 1975.
A qualified chartered accountant, he started his practice in 1971 before moving into pharma.
forbes_facts: Godha hails from a family of farmers.
He is a patron of the Jain International Trade Organization, which runs training centres for students preparing for the civil services.

name: Artem Khachatryan
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2021-2025); Hurun Global (2022-2026)
forbes_bio: Artem Khachatryan cofounded Russian discount retailer Fix Price in 2007 together with Sergei Lomakin.
The chain has opened more than 4,000 stores across Russia, Kazakhstan, Georgia, Belarus, Latvia, Kyrgyzstan and Uzbekistan.
Khachatryan was previously the executive director of the company, which went public in 2021.
In December 2023 Khachatryan sold his entire stake in FixPrice and resigned as a member of the board, citing family matters.
His cofounder, Lomakin, is also a billionaire.

name: JB Straubel
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2025); Hurun Global (2026); Hurun Unicorn founders (2021-2026)
forbes_bio: JB Straubel is the founder and CEO of Redwood Materials and the former chief technology officer of Tesla.
A Stanford-educated engineer, Straubel was working on battery-powered planes in 2003 when he met Elon Musk at a campus lecture.
He joined Tesla as employee No. 5 in 2004, and drove the development of its battery packs and electric motors as CTO. He left the C-suite in 2019 but remains on the board.
He now runs Redwood Materials, a Nevada-based electric vehicle battery recycling startup  he founded in 2017.

He now runs Redwood Materials, a Nevada-based electric vehicle battery recycling startup he founded in 2017. It has since expanded to making battery materials from recovered metals. In 2025, Redwood also began building and selling battery storage systems for data centers..

name: Zhao Mantang

name: Andrew Tisch
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2024-2025); Hurun Global (2025-2026); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Andrew Tisch's father Laurence (d. 2003) started Loews Corporation with his brother Bob (d. 2005) as a New Jersey hotel venture in 1946.
Andrew co-chairs Loews with his cousin Jonathan. His brother James is CEO.
Loews is active in insurance, drilling rigs, natural gas pipelines and hotels.
Andrew's mother Wilma is also a billionaire, as are his cousins Laurie and Steven.
The Tisch family donated funds to support NYU's Tisch School of the Arts and its Tisch Hospital at Langone Medical Center.

name: Paul Van Zuydam
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Hurun Global (2026)
forbes_bio: Paul Van Zuydam is the owner and chairman of Le Creuset, a cookware company known for its colorful enameled cast-iron pots.
Van Zuydam acquired Le Creuset in 1988, quitting his job to buy the company himself after a deal he had championed for his then-employer fell through.
Le Creuset was founded in 1925 by two Belgians in Fresnoy-le-Grand, a small village in northern France.
Today, the company brings in more than $700 million in revenue and produces around 10,000 cast iron products a day in its France-based factory.
forbes_facts: Paul's son, Paulo Van Zuydam, is the director of the company.
Flame, a gradient red and orange color, is the original color of Le Creuset.

name: Fernando Espinosa Abdalá
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2024-2025); Hurun Global (2025-2026)
forbes_bio: Fernando Espinosa Abdalá and his brother Leopoldo derive much of their fortune from the sale of their drug manufacturer Rimsa, which it sold to Tel Aviv-based Teva Pharmaceuticals for $2.3 billion.
Fernando was the operational president of the company before the sale in 2016.
Their father founded the business in 1970 as a pharmaceutical distributor before expanding into manufacturing.
Following the sale, Teva sued Fernando and Leopoldo claiming fraud and a breach of contract.
Most of the charges were dismissed; as for breach of contract, the parties eventually settled for less than $200 million.

name: Robert Knauf
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2021-2025)
forbes_bio: Robert Matthias Knauf is an heir to one of the world's leading producers of building materials and systems, Knauf Gips KG.
Based in Iphofen, Germany, the company employs more than 35,000 people around the world and has annual revenue of over $11 billion.
Its product line includes plasterboards, cement boards and insulating materials.
Knauf Gips dates to 1932, when brothers and mining engineers Alfons and Karl Knauf obtained rights to gypsum deposits in Schengen, Germany.
Their original gypsum factory, on the Moselle River in the border region of Luxembourg, Germany and France, is still the company's production nucleus.
forbes_facts: The family's Knauf Museum, on the premises of a historical inn built in 1688 on Iphofen's market square, houses a renowned collection or ancient relief art.

name: Jorge Feffer
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2019-2025); Hurun Global (2019-2026)
forbes_bio: Jorge Feffer is one of four billionaire brothers who control Suzano, a Brazilian paper giant founded by their grandfather.
In January 2019, Suzano completed a roughly $7.5 billion acquisition of Brazilian pulp and paper maker Fibria.
He was the Deputy Chief Corporate Officer of Suzano from 2013 until 2015.
Jorge partnered with a Brazilian publisher on a book series known as Library of Social Critics, with works by authors like philosopher Leo Strauss.
His grandfather, a Ukrainian immigrant, founded the company in 1924.
